name: flame.computer/close.v1
description: Human-only: revoke the exact control session, cancel pending permissions and execution, and join its original engine. Already dispatched external effects cannot be undone.

name: flame.computer/context.v1
description: Read the current worker identity and original runtime instructions and js/js_reset schemas before execution. This never opens a session or grants application access.

name: flame.computer/execute.v1
description: Execute js or js_reset on the exact accepted worker and surface. Arguments follow the captured upstream schema. An observed result is durable; transport loss never authorizes replay. Reset discards the original JavaScript heap.

name: flame.computer/history.v1
description: Read original operation headers in admission order, newest first. This is a projection of durable receipts, not an execution log with a second owner.

name: flame.computer/open.v1
description: Human-only: open one exclusive computer-control session on the Runtime host for the stated lease. Existing sessions are not replaced; expiry cancels and closes the engine.

name: flame.computer/read.v1
description: Read the actual Runtime host and current computer-control session. This does not start an engine or authorize computer access.

name: flame.computer/reply.v1
description: Human-only: answer the exact live upstream permission request. The original runtime owns allowed scopes; cancelled, settled or replaced requests cannot be answered.

name: flame.computer/result.v1
description: Read original input, identity and the one observed outcome. An absent outcome means unconfirmed; this method never executes or infers desktop effects.

name: flame.computer/stop.v1
description: Human-only: interrupt the exact current operation and retire its engine before any later operation can run. A missing original result remains unknown.

name: flame.computer/watch.v1
description: Observe bounded complete snapshots of the computer-control owner. Disconnecting this observation does not close the session.
